title: The distinction between essence and accident in knowledge and soul
english: It accepts more and less. Therefore, it can sometimes be cast away and sometimes taken up. But that which is hot in fire does not accept more and less, for it is not essential. The knowledge of God is essential, so it is incommensurable with knowledge according to disposition. And the incommensurable things do not accept likeness.

These things are not said in vain; for since the Logos constructs the Son to be consubstantial with the Father and [establishes] the same divinity through the being known by the Father and knowing the Father, they wish to share his knowledge with ours, saying: 'Just as we know God, and he knows, that we know him perfectly, as he knows himself. And the Son likewise has the knowledge concerning him. Therefore he will not rule us.' 27 Their hearts shall live unto ages of ages.

Often things that have happened are called homonymously by those to whom they have happened. We say that there is an essence of the soul; when God says, 'Do not fear those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul' (Matt 10:28). Thus the name 'soul' denotes essence. And when he says, 'Spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord' (Ps 146:20), it denotes essence. For the name of the soul often signifies something that has happened to the soul; for when it is said in Jesus Wisdom: 'An evil soul will destroy the one who has acquired it,' it names the disposition and the intellect 'soul'; for the one who has acquired it, the soul, is the man. And again: 'Having reached those near, in the obedience of the truth.' From this it is also nicknamed, 'You, man, are equal-souled to me,' the one having the same choice as me. And again, if it is said: 'And eat grapes as much as you will fill the soul,' it speaks of the appetitive power as 'soul' in this way.

Not all then the things said denote the underlying essences, but there is also when it signifies things that have happened to them. And it has happened to man to know God. Therefore, it is not said 'knowledge' of the man, but 'knowing.' Here the thing that happened is not homonymous with the underlying thing. But the Savior is called both wise and wisdom, and having knowledge and knowledge, and righteousness and righteous; and I do not say here 'happened' and 'underlying,' but through two parallel names, the same.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Immortality of the Soul and Heart
english: It is signified: for if I say that the Savior is righteousness, I do not say him as a person, nor as a disposition; and if I say him just—'but you have denied the just one' (Matt 23:35)—I do not say the one who performs [it], but the righteousness. Thus also we say of God in general. I do not say that God is just in the sense of participating in righteousness, but in the sense of providing righteousness. And the soul according to essence does not receive the more or the less. But that soul, by which some are called beautiful-souled, does receive [it]. Therefore, the disposition is called 'soul' in the same way as the essence.

The heart and the mind mean the same thing; for when it is said: 'Where your treasure is, there also your heart will be' (Matt 6:21), there also is your mind. 'Blessed are the pure in heart' (Matt 5:8). Therefore, to say mind and heart is the same. Not concerning all things, however, but concerning men. See: the soul and the mind of man are immortal. If it is immortal, it is sought, or it is something else and another thing.

And the sinner, having an immortal soul, is never destroyed; for one should not pay attention to those saying that the souls of the wicked turn into non-existence, as the Stoics wish among the Greeks, and the Hieracites among the Christians. Therefore the soul is immortal and has a natural life according to which it is moved. And the sinner also has this life according to which he is immortal.

He does not speak now about this natural life saying: 'their hearts shall live' (Ps 42:5)—but according to that life which the believer has and the one knowing God has. If the hearts live unto the age of ages according to the blessed life, it is evident that they also remain always according to the essential life, which is common to sinners and to the diligent. And just as I say that everyone has sight when animals have sight, I say that the one seeing well previously had sight; for he would not have seen well if he did not have the seeing, and again he would not have seen badly if he did not have the seeing. Therefore both the soul and the heart have life forever, whether it be wicked or diligent. And natural life anticipates; for he would not have been able to live according to God and to live according to faith, if he were not immortal, if he did not have essential life. Therefore the hearts of these, those having eaten and having been filled, those fearing God and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Eternal Life and the Return of the Nations
english: Those praising him shall live not for one age, but 'for the age of ages.' A multitude of ages is signified; for he did not say 'for one age,' but 'for the age of ages.' And just as 'Sabbaths of Sabbaths' is said and 'years of years' for those many years which are the days of a year, so he shall live 'for the age of ages.'

All the ends of the earth shall be remembered and shall turn back to the Lord. He prophesies concerning the salvation of all mankind; for it is necessary that that which is spoken of be brought to pass, about which this holy one says again in another psalm: 'all the nations, all whom you have made, shall come and worship before you' (Psalm 22:27). For God did not make the rational beings so that they might sin, by standing up against Him to worship these things, but so that they might honor God. And since this is the purpose of the Creator, but a purpose of those who have come to be has intervened, the purpose of God must prevail. Therefore, when He is remembered, we provide the cause for being remembered; for He remembers those who remember, as He knows those who are attentive. When we remember, then He remembers us and calls us into salvation. The 'they shall turn back' shows that no one is evil by essence, but by choice. If the evil was able to diminish the choice toward something else, the good will be able to call it back to its former state.

And all the patriarchies of the nations shall worship before Him. After the turning back, they worship. They do not worship first and then turn back; thus it signifies progress. And it is a great thing to worship before God. He who worships Him as is fitting worships before Him. Therefore, the reason: 'because' the kingdom is His. He says 'kingdom' here, not the beginning, but those who are being ruled, as it is said: 'in the gathering of peoples together and the kingdoms of serving the Lord.' If they were bad by construction, they would have been something else.

And He Himself is the master of the nations. Since the kingdom is His and He Himself has made the nations, He is their master. Therefore, they turn back to their own master. They do not enrich God by turning back; for they are His.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
